fieldDescription: How much of a tactical or saturation bombardment's damage gets through a functional planetary shield. A shield that is already disrupted absorbs nothing - and the bombardment itself disrupts the shield, so repeated strikes will eventually land unmitigated.
Fraction of bombardment-caused industry disruption time that gets through the shield. 0.5 = disruption durations halved. 0 = fully absorbed. 1 = vanilla.
Fraction of the bombardment's stability hit (recent unrest) that gets through the shield. 0.5 = halved. 0 = fully absorbed. 1 = vanilla.
A functional shield prevents the permanent pollution condition a bombardment would otherwise add to a habitable world.
The shield's hard guarantees: what a functional shield outright prevents.
A functional shield prevents the colony-size reduction from a saturation bombardment.

A colony with a functional shield cannot be decivilized - neither by saturation bombardment nor by stability collapse. (Implemented via the story-critical market flag; if you uninstall the mod, disable this option and load+save once first so the flag is cleaned up.)
Who benefits, and what the shield gives up in exchange.
Restore the vanilla x3 ground-defense bonus (plus alpha-core and improvement bonuses). Off by default: the shield stops bombs, not marines.
Only protect player-owned colonies. Off = any market with a functional planetary shield benefits - including NPC markets you bombard yourself.
Show a message when a shield absorbs a bombardment over one of your colonies.
Logs shield snapshots, bombardment detection, and mitigation math to starsector.log (prefix [UPS]).
